text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German debt markets were closed for the New Year holiday. The March bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.79, down 0.01 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended unchanged in very thin trading in the last trading session of the year. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-30/32, unchanged from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures ended the year on a sour note as stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data upset bond markets in thin trading conditions ahead of the New Year holiday. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.30 down 1.00 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended the year on a bullish note with the March Btp contract on LIFFE touching a new record high in a market buoyed by hopes of an end to a long-running Italian metalworkers' pay dispute and a resulting cut in the Bank of Italy's key interest rates, traders said. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.40, up 0.85 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury securities prices fell sharply following the release of much stronger-than-expected new home sales figures. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-29/32, down 31/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.63 percent.
JAPAN - Japanese bonds were closed. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 124.26, up 0.05 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw no activity with most European centres closed for the New Year holiday and others open for a half-day only. January 1 is a market holiday and Eurobond business will resume on Thursday.
DSL Finance NV plans to issue a 1.0 billion mark ($645 million) 10-year Eurobond on January 2, via joint lead managers Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and SBC Warburg.
Dealers said the 10-year mark sector looked favourable, with the European Investment Bank, KfW and Austria also mooted. Jumbo dollar bonds were also likely in the coming weeks. ($1=1.5504 Mark)
